name: Navadvīpa-dhāma
aka: Navadvipa, Nabadwip, Navadvīpa, Nadīyā, Nadia, Śrī Navadvīpa-dhāma
location: Lat. 23°24', long. 88°24'. Nine islands on both banks of the Gaṅgā, a little over 42 square miles
about:
The abode of Śrī Gaura. A capital of the Sena kings and the foremost centre of Sanskrit learning in Bengal: Ballāla Sena's palace was at Śimuliyā (Brāhmaṇapukur); under Lakṣmaṇa Sena poetry on Kṛṣṇa-līlā flourished (the Gīta-govinda was sung at his court), and Navadvīpa kept its lead in nyāya and tantra until the mid-19th century.
The nine islands — east of the present Gaṅgā: (1) Antardvīpa: old Māyāpur, Bhāruiḍāṅgā, the Nidayā ghāṭ (Mahāprabhu crossed here on his way to Kāṭwā); (2) Sīmantadvīpa: Bāmunpukur, Saraḍāṅgā, Ballāladīghi, Simuliyā (Sīmantinī Devī); (3) Godrumadvīpa: Gādigāchā, Suvarṇavihāra, Svarūpagañja; (4) Madhyadvīpa: Mājidā. West of the Gaṅgā: (5) Koladvīpa: Kuliyā or Kolera, south of Teghari, Samudragaḍa, Cāṁpāhāṭi; (6) Ṛtudvīpa: Rātupur and Vidyānagara; (7) Modadrumadvīpa: Māugāchi (Māmagāchi), Mahatpur, Brahmāṇītalā; (8) Jahnudvīpa: Jānnagara, Pāruliyā, Julu; (9) Rudradvīpa: Rāhupur (Rudraḍāṅgā), Śaṅkarapur, Pūrvasthalī.
Where old Navadvīpa stood is disputed: the Abhidhāna notes contrary views (Sundarānanda Vidyāvinoda held that the present Navadvīpa town is Kuliyā).
In the present town the Abhidhāna lists, among others: the house of Kholāvecā Śrīdhara in the weavers' quarter; Poḍā-mā (the goddess worshipped by the young Vāsudeva Sārvabhauma); the Gaura deity installed by Viṣṇupriyā Devī with the help of Vaṁśīvadana Ṭhākura (her wooden sandals are on the throne; served by the descendants of her brother Yādavācārya); the Maṇipur palace (Rāja Bhāgyacandra Siṁha, 1799, with his daughter Lāiroibī: the Anu-Mahāprabhu deity). Samādhis and āśramas of siddhas: Totārāma dāsa Bābājī (Baḍa ākhaḍā; his Śyāmasundara), Vaṁśīdāsa Bābājī (north of Baḍāl ghāṭ), Gaurakiśora dāsa Bābājī, Caitanya dāsa Bābājī (by Mahāprabhu's temple), Jagannātha dāsa Bābājī (samādhi and bhajana-kuṭīra), Rādhāramaṇa-caraṇa dāsa Bābājī and Gaurahari dāsa Bābājī (by the Śrīvāsāṅgana ghāṭ), Rādhācaraṇa dāsa Bābājī.

name: Māyāpur
region: Nadīyā, West Bengal (east bank of the Gaṅgā)
location: In Antardvīpa, one of the nine islands of Navadvīpa
about: Within Śrī Navadvīpa (Bhakti-ratnākara 6.131, 8.72, 12.56, 83–87): the appearance place of Śrī Gaurasundara, the great Yogapīṭha, non-different from Śrī Vṛndāvana. Antardvīpa holds old Māyāpur, Bhāruiḍāṅgā (where Dewān Gaṅgāgovinda Siṁha's old temple stood) and the Nidayā ghāṭ, where Mahāprabhu crossed the Gaṅgā on his way to Kāṭwā to take sannyāsa.

name: Sīmantadvīpa
aka: Simantadvipa, Śimuliyā, Simuliya, Bāmunpukur, Brāhmaṇapukur, Ballāladīghi
region: Nadīyā, West Bengal (Navadvīpa, east of the Gaṅgā)
about:
One of the nine islands of Navadvīpa (Caitanya-bhāgavata Madhya 23.300). North of Brāhmaṇapukur is the pīṭha of Sīmantinī Devī. Ballāla Sena's palace stood here: the Ballāla-ḍhibi mound and the Ballāla-dīghi tank remain. Chānd Kāzī's house was at Brāhmaṇapukur.
Saraḍāṅgā (Rājāpura or Saraḍāṅgā), north of Kājīnagara: Śrī Jagannātha is served; the kings of the Sura line lived here.

name: Chānd Kāzī's samādhi
aka: Chand Kazi, Cānda Kājī, Kājira samādhi, Kājīnagara, Kazi samadhi
location: Across the present Gaṅgā, near the bazar, about three miles north of the confluence of the Gaṅgā and the Khaḍiyā
about: The samādhi of the Kāzī (Chānd Kāzī) whom Mahāprabhu met in the saṅkīrtana movement (Caitanya-bhāgavata Madhya 23.359–379). Some say he was a grandson of Hussain Shāh, the badshah of Gauḍa; others that he was Hussain Shāh's guru, the governor of the region, or the faujdār of Navadvīpa. The samādhi is under a golaka-cāṁpā tree outside his house, inside a low wall; behind it stood his house, and a stone from it lies in the courtyard. The ruins of the Kājīnagara can still be seen. Nearby is the grave of Maulānā Sirājuddīn.

name: Godrumadvīpa
region: Nadīyā, West Bengal (Navadvīpa, east of the Gaṅgā)
about: One of the nine islands of Navadvīpa. At Suvarṇavihāra are the remains of a Sena king's house; kings of the Pāla line also ruled here.

name: Madhyadvīpa
region: Nadīyā, West Bengal (Navadvīpa, east of the Gaṅgā)
location: The village of Mājidā, on the east bank of the Gaṅgā
about: One of the nine islands of Navadvīpa. Near Mājidā, in the Haṁsavāhana bil, is Śrī Haṁsavāhana Śiva, who comes up for three days at Caitra saṅkrānti. South of Brāhmaṇapāḍā (Brāhmaṇapurā), at Depāḍā (Devapallī), there is an old Nṛsiṁhadeva.

name: Kuliyā
aka: Kuliya, Koladvīpa, Koladvipa, Kolera, Sātakuliyā, Kuliyā-Pāhāḍapura
region: Nadīyā, West Bengal (Navadvīpa, west of the Gaṅgā)
location: In Koladvīpa: Kuliyā or Kolera, south of Teghari
about: Kuliyā (Sātakuliyā, «Kuliyā-Pāhāḍapura»): Mādhava dāsa lived here, and Mahāprabhu stayed in his house (some say this Mādhava dāsa was of Kulīnagrāma). Koladvīpa, one of the nine islands, takes in Kuliyā or Kolera, the land south of Teghari, Samudragaḍa and Cāṁpāhāṭi. Sundarānanda Vidyāvinoda held that the present Navadvīpa town is Kuliyā.

name: Samudragaḍa
about: A deity of Mahāprabhu and Lachmanjīu are here. It was the capital of King Samudrasena; others say the home of Samudra Gupta. Siddheśvarī is worshipped at Samudragaḍa.

name: Vidyānagara
region: Nadīyā / Bardhamān, West Bengal (Navadvīpa, west of the Gaṅgā)
location: In Ṛtudvīpa, north of Dakṣiṇa Pāṭī; one kroś from Jānnagara
about: The houses of Vāsudeva Sārvabhauma and of Gaṅgādāsa Paṇḍita stood here; Mahāprabhu used to come here to study. Ṛtudvīpa, one of the nine islands, takes in Rātupur (Rāhutapur) and Vidyānagara.

name: Māmagāchi
region: Bardhamān, West Bengal (Navadvīpa, west of the Gaṅgā)
about: Modadrumadvīpa, one of the nine islands (Māugāchi, Mahatpur, Brahmāṇītalā). Three śrīpāṭas here: (1) of Sāraṅga Murāri Prabhu, with the service of Śrī Rādhā-Gopīnātha and an old bakula tree; (2) of Śrīmatī Nārāyaṇī Devī; (3) of Vāsudeva Datta — the Rādhā-Madanagopāla he served is now served at Sāraṅga Murāri's śrīpāṭa.

name: Jānnagara
region: Bardhamān, West Bengal (Navadvīpa, west of the Gaṅgā)
location: In Jahnudvīpa (Jānnagara, Pāruliyā, Julu); one kroś from Vidyānagara
about: Here, it is said, Jahnu Muni drank the Gaṅgā in one sip; his āśrama stood on the bank of the old Gaṅgā, and a little south of it is Bhīṣmadeva's mound. The Bhāgīrathī once flowed on the east side of Jānnagara. In 1846 there were ten large temples and a hundred ṭols here. Half a kroś west is Rākṣasī-potā, the palace of Rāja Candra Siṁha.

name: Belpukur
location: On the north bank of the old Gaṅgā (the Guḍaguḍe)
about: The home of Nīlāmbara Cakravartī (the Abhidhāna places Belpukur in Rudradvīpa). A place where Kṛṣṇa grazed the cows; Lakṣmī performed austerities here.

name: Mālañcapāḍā
about: The house of Sanātana Miśra stood here: the birthplace of Viṣṇupriyā Devī. An old guluñca tree is still a witness of the past.
